Subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint — data access, retention & deployment decisions

Hi John / Acme team —

Following up from Friday's demo: this week’s MAP checkpoint focused on two outstanding items from the security & deployment workstream:

1) Preferred deployment mode (VPC vs. on-prem) and blockers
2) Data retention and PII handling for the pilot dataset

I’ve attached an evaluation matrix (redwood-data-eval-matrix.xlsx) and the completed portion of your questionnaire (acme-data-questionnaire.pdf). Please review the proposal below so we can lock owners and timelines on Wednesday's cadence call.

Summary proposal (requested decision items):
- Deployment: run pilot in our Dedicated VPC environment with optional on-prem connector for sensitive subsets.
- Data access: pilot ingestion via SFTP into a customer-isolated bucket (no shared logs).
- Retention: 30-day token-level logs retained in customer account; raw input retention = 7 days unless explicitly flagged for retention by Acme IT.
- PII handling: automated redaction for user identifiers + manual review flag for records containing regulated identifiers (SSNs, gov IDs).

Immediate asks for this week:
- Acme: confirm whether any pilot records are subject to regulatory hold or must remain on-prem (owner: John Dow, due Tue EOD).
- Redwood: provide a short runbook for the VPC ingestion flow and access controls (owner: Karthik Iyer, due Wed 11:59am).
- Joint: finalize retention SLA text for the contract addendum (owner: Monica Patel / Acme Legal, due Thu).

If those timelines work I’ll update the MAP worksheet and circulate a short mutual checklist prior to the call.

Thanks —
Evelyn

John —

Thanks for the quick note. Short technical summary below — I’ll also add this to the Drive link and the MAP worksheet.

Architecture options (summary):
- Dedicated VPC (recommended for pilot): Acme has an isolated VPC with customer-managed buckets. Ingestion via SFTP -> customer bucket; Redwood instances in the Dedicated pool access the bucket over private networking. Logs and token-level events are written to a customer-owned storage endpoint (no shared Red server logs).
- On-prem connector (optional): a lightweight bridge you run inside your network that performs model calls via mutually authenticated TLS to a Redwood gateway. The connector can:
  - route regulated records to a local-only inference path (no egress), or
  - forward redacted payloads to the Dedicated VPC for full processing.

Data retention controls we can support out-of-the-box:
- Default token log retention configurable at the account level (7/14/30/90 days).
- Flagging: records can be tagged at ingest; flagged records follow a different retention policy.
- PII redaction: Redwood offers pre-ingest redaction heuristics + a review workflow that quarantines flagged records for manual approval.

Proposed next steps (owners & dates):
- Karthik -> Deliver VPC runbook + connector architecture diagram (attachment to Drive) — due Wed 2027-02-10 11:59am PT.
- John -> Confirm regulated-set list and whether run-in on-prem is required — due Tue 2027-02-09 EOD.
- Monica -> Draft contract addendum language for 14/30-day retention options for Acme to review — due Thu 2027-02-11 EOD.

If we get John’s decision on the regulated set by Tue, we can agree whether the pilot will run mixed-mode (most data in Dedicated VPC; regulated set handled locally).

Karthik

John / team —

Appreciate the heads-up on the regulated subset. Based on the info so far we’ll propose two contract addendum options you can choose from:

Option A (mixed mode):
- Pilot runs in Dedicated VPC for non-regulated data.
- Regulated subset remains on-prem via connector with no egress; Redwood will provide telemetry-only metrics (aggregate counts) for those records.
- Retention: 14 days for employee PII by default; 30 days for token logs if Acme opts in.

Option B (redaction-first):
- All records routed to Dedicated VPC after pre-ingest PII redaction. Regulated records are redacted to remove prohibited identifiers before transfer.
- Retention: 7 days default for redacted payloads; 30 days optional for token logs.

Please confirm which option Acme prefers so we can finalize the MAP and update the mutual checklist. If you prefer, Monica and I can set a short legal/IT sync tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks —
